title: In 1935, 102 Toads Became Over 200 Million in Australia

scenes.text: In 1935, Australia imported cane toads to protect its sugar cane.
Scientists brought 102 from Hawaii, bred them, and released about 2,400.
A female can lay up to 30,000 eggs in one batch. Native frogs lay about 2,000.
Their skin is poisonous enough to kill animals that bite them.
Today, there are over 200 million cane toads in Australia.

description:
102 toads turned into over 200 million.
In 1935 cane toads were brought to Queensland to protect sugar cane. About 2,400 were released, and a female lays up to 30,000 eggs at once. Estimates now say over 200 million toads live in Australia.
Can you think of a worse way to fix a problem? Tell us below.
first_comment: Native frogs lay about 2,000 eggs a year. A cane toad can lay 30,000 in one clutch. Would you have stopped the release?
